narrative.text:
NARRATIVE:

ENCOUNTER:

On May 1, 2017, at approximately 12:06 PM, [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] Border Patrol Station received a call from an FBI Task Force Agent. Border Patrol Agent [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] informed agents from the [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] Border Patrol Station that he had arrested [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] (COB: Honduras, DOB: [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] ) for being present in the United States without immigration documents.

Border Patrol Agent [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] responded to the [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] located at [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] in Avon, Ohio and took custody of the subject. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] was transported to the [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] Border Patrol Station for processing. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] was read and understood his Miranda Rights in the Spanish Language at approximately 1:35 PM. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] declined to speak to agents without the presence of an attorney as documented on the I-214. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] signed and consented to the search of his personal cellular phone as documented on the "Consent to Search Cell Phone" form.

PROCESSING INFORMATION:

At the station, [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] fingerprints and photograph were entered into the [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] databases which returned with the following results.

IMMIGRATION HISTORY:

None

CRIMINAL HISTORY:

None

TRAVEL/WORK:

[REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] stated that he left his home city of Azacualpa in the state of Santa Barbara, Honduras, on or about 06/14/2009. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] stated that he travelled by bus for approximately one day before arriving in Naco, Mexico. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] stated that he used the services of a local smuggler to help him safely cross the US/Mexico Border. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] stated that he paid approximately $5,000.00 USD to illegally cross the border. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] stated that he and five others crossed the US/MEXICO Border illegally, into Naco, Arizona, on the afternoon of 06/15/2009. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] stated that they walked for five days and were picked-up by an unknown driver. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] stated that he was driven to Orlando, Florida where he lived for a year. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] claims he moved to Ohio due to the high cost of living in Florida. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] stated he lived and continues to live with his girlfriend at [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] in Lorain, Ohio. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] stated that he has been working in construction since his arrival into the United States and is currently working for [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] in West Lake, Ohio. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] failed to provide a detailed account of his travel and work history.

DISPOSITION:

A Notice to Appear is being executed on [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] as per section 212(a)(6)(A)(I) of the Immigration and Nationality Act. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] and his property will be held at the [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] County Jail for the duration of his immigration proceedings. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] was advised of his right to speak with a consular officer of his native country of Honduras, which he declined. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] was provided with a list of Legal Services and Consulate contact information.

[REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] did not claim any fear of returning to his home country of Honduras. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] was not offered a bond. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] claims and appeared to be in good health at the time of his processing. Upon service of paperwork, [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] refused to sign any forms.
